title: The example role matrix has orchestrator rows and a Codex implementer alternative
lead: `relay-roles init` writes an example matrix whose `recommend` resolves every role, the orchestrator included, on a fresh project: a Claude Code orchestrator first, a Codex one second, and a Codex implementer alternative after the Claude implementer rows. Default picks for every role stay on Claude Code.
findings_note: s320 relay 2026-10-16 owner question: the relay-roles init example has no orchestrator row, so recommend leaves the orchestrator unmatched on a fresh project; owner chose Claude and Codex orchestrator rows plus a Codex implementer alternative
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the example's rules (the eight rule texts stay as they are, including "No cross-vendor reviewer unless the owner asks"); Codex reviewer, gate or architect rows; changing any existing matrix (only `init` and `init --force` write the example); launching or verifying Codex sessions (the agents repo owns that); bumping the relay contract marker, since the example's rows are data the Setup reads, not a rule an outer session follows.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
s320 (landed 2026-10-16) added the `orchestrator` role and changed the relay Setup to say `recommend` "resolves every role, the orchestrator included, to one row" (`src/slicer/ai.py:385`). Its spec forbade changing the generic example's vendor policy, so `roles.skeleton()` (`src/slicer/roles.py:407`) still holds eight Claude Code rows and no orchestrator row, and `docs/agents.md:101` says so. On a fresh project `recommend` prints `orchestrator  (no matching row)` and its JSON reports `"unmatched": ["orchestrator"]`, so the owner picks the orchestrator by hand and the Setup text is wrong for every new project. The owner decided on 2026-10-16 to change the example's vendor policy: add a Claude Code orchestrator and a Codex orchestrator, plus a Codex implementer alternative, as this project's own matrix does (r9, r10, r11).

Scores: importance 2 because every fresh project starts with an unmatched role and Setup text that does not hold; urgency 1 because only a new `init` or `init --force` is affected and the owner can add rows by hand; effort 1 and size S because it is three rows in one function plus the docs and tests that pin the example. Tree slicer, pass v1.13 beside the other relay follow-ups. Discovered from s320.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/roles.py`: `skeleton()`. The inner `row()` helper hardcodes `agent="Claude Code", vendor="Claude"`; give it `agent` and `vendor` keywords with those defaults. Update its docstring ("Every row runs on one agent" no longer holds).
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py`: `test_Skeleton_FirstRowAndFirstRule_NumberTheExampleFromThere` (row id lists, `next_row` 16 becomes 19), `test_Skeleton_HoldsEightStructuredRowsAndEightRules` (rename for eleven rows), and any other test that pins the row list.
- `tests/test_merge_roles.py`: the tests that run `relay-roles init` and then pin added row ids and `next_row` (around lines 494 to 523, which expect `r9`, `r10` and `(11, 11)`); the added rows will be numbered after r11.
- `tests/test_ai.py` only if a test pins row text beyond `render_markdown(roles.skeleton())`.
- `docs/commands.md`: the `relay-roles init` row (line 59: "eight rows ... all on the agent `Claude Code`") and the `relay-roles add` row (line 60: the next id in a fresh example is `r9`, which becomes `r12`).
- `docs/agents.md`: line 101 ("has no orchestrator row") and line 86 if its description of the example's implementer rows needs the new row.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Skeleton_HoldsElevenStructuredRowsAndEightRules`: rows in order `r8, r1, r2, r3, r4, r9, r5, r6, r7, r10, r11`. r9 is implementer, no conditions, `Codex / OpenAI / gpt-6.1-sol / medium`, note "alternate implementer for any slice, split part or sliver". r10 is orchestrator, no conditions, `Claude Code / Claude / opus / high`, note "default orchestrator". r11 is orchestrator, no conditions, `Codex / OpenAI / gpt-6.1-sol / high`, note "alternate orchestrator". Rules unchanged.
- `test_RelayRolesRecommend_FreshExample_ResolvesEveryRole`: after `relay-roles init`, `recommend --well-specified yes --split no --json` on an S effort-1 item has `unmatched == []`, picks Claude Code for all five roles (implementer r1, orchestrator r10), and lists r9 among the implementer alternatives and r11 as the orchestrator alternative.
- `test_RelayRolesRecommend_FreshExamplePreferCodex_PicksCodexRows`: the same with `--prefer-agent Codex` picks r9 and r11 by `preferred_agent`; reviewer, gate and architect keep their Claude rows by `matrix_order`.
- The existing first-row test with `first_row=8` numbers the new rows r16, r17, r18 and `next_row` is 19.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the three rows to `skeleton()` with their numbers: `row(9, ...)` listed after `row(4, ...)`, and `row(10, ...)`, `row(11, ...)` after `row(7, ...)`, so r1 to r8 keep their ids and meaning. Defaults are preserved because matrix order decides and a Claude Code implementer row always matches first (r3 for any whole slice, r4 for any split part, r8 for any sliver).
3. Update the docs and tests named under Files, and add the CHANGELOG entry. Mutation-check: dropping r10 must turn the fresh-example recommend test red.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full discover. `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- On a scratch project outside the repo: `slicer relay-roles init`, then `slicer relay-roles recommend ID --well-specified yes --split no` lists a row for every role.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
